formal_proof: Metaphysical Grounding (SEP): No entity can metaphysically ground itself (¬(x ≺ x)). Proved via strict non-circular dependency rules.
context_description: Axiom stating that grounding relation is irreflexive; nothing is the source of its own existence.

formal_proof: Metaphysical Grounding (SEP): If x grounds y, then y does not ground x (x ≺ y → ¬(y ≺ x)). Proved via strict hierarchical dependency priority.
context_description: Axiom stating that grounding is asymmetric; dependence is unidirectional.

formal_proof: Metaphysical Grounding (SEP): If x grounds y and y grounds z, then x grounds z (x ≺ y ∧ y ≺ z → x ≺ z). Proved via deductive inheritance of dependency.
context_description: Axiom stating that grounding is transitive; intermediate dependencies preserve ultimate grounding.

formal_proof: Philosophy of Time (SEP): Only presently existing entities exist. Past entities did exist, and future entities will exist, but do not exist now.
context_description: Temporal metaphysics theory restricting ontology strictly to the present.

formal_proof: Philosophy of Time (SEP): Past, present, and future entities all exist equally. Time is a four-dimensional block where temporal location does not affect ontological status.
context_description: Temporal metaphysics theory treating past, present, and future as equally real.

formal_proof: Philosophy of Time (SEP): The past and the present exist, but the future does not exist yet. The block of reality grows continuously as new moments become present.
context_description: Temporal metaphysics theory stating the past and present are real, but the future is non-existent.

formal_proof: Mind-Body Metaphysics (SEP): There is only one material substance (physical matter), but it possesses two distinct and irreducible classes of properties: physical and mental.
context_description: Non-reductive mind-body theory asserting mental properties are fundamental and irreducible.

formal_proof: Mind-Body Metaphysics (SEP): Physical events in the brain cause mental events (consciousness), but mental events have no physical causal influence on the brain or behavior.
context_description: Theory stating that mind is a causally impotent byproduct of physical brain processes.

formal_proof: Mind-Body Metaphysics (SEP): The ultimate reality is neither mental nor physical, but consists of a neutral substance whose manifestations appear as mental or physical.
context_description: Theory asserting reality is composed of a single, neutral kind of substance.

formal_proof: Mind-Body Metaphysics (SEP): Reality is fundamentally mental or immaterial. The physical world is either a projection of individual minds or a manifestation of a universal mind.
context_description: Theory asserting that existence is fundamentally spiritual or mental.

formal_proof: Metaphysics of Causation (SEP): An event C causes event E by directly initiating the causal chain, preempting an alternative event A which would have caused E otherwise.
context_description: Axiom distinguishing direct causation from backup potential causes.

formal_proof: Metaphysics of Causation (SEP): An event E is caused by multiple independent, sufficient causes C1 and C2 simultaneously, where each alone would have been sufficient for E.
context_description: Axiom defining scenarios with redundant sufficient causes.
